export.about: Jump timings marked by hand, frame by frame, on videos in Airtime. Each session is one video. Marks are the source data; everything under "derived", "tables" and "overview" is computed from them and can be recomputed. For analysis across sessions, start with "tables": flat rows that load directly into a dataframe or chart. Sessions are ordered by recordedAt, oldest first.

fields.sessions[].marks[].seconds: Media time of the mark in seconds (source of truth). Snapped to a frame boundary.
fields.sessions[].marks[].frame: Frame index, derived as round(seconds × frameRate.value).
fields.sessions[].marks[].type: "takeoff" = last frame a toe still touches the ground; "landing" = first frame the feet touch down.
fields.sessions[].frameRate: Frames per second used for frame math. source: "container" = read from the file, "playback-estimate" = measured during playback, "default" = 30 fps assumed by an older version of Airtime because the frame rate could not be read or measured.
fields.sessions[].jumpType: What kind of jump the session holds, one per session: "approach", "drop-jump" or "repeat-hops". null = not set: saved before jump types existed, or with a type that is no longer offered. Compare like with like. An approach jump's contact is its plant step.
fields.sessions[].timeScale: Real seconds per media second. 1 = real-time footage; 0.25 = 4× slow motion.
fields.sessions[].derived.intervals[]: Consecutive takeoff→landing pairs are "flight", landing→takeoff pairs are "contact". A flight runs from the takeoff frame (the last on the floor) to the landing frame (frames = landing frame − takeoff frame). A contact runs from its landing frame to the first frame in the air, the one after the takeoff (frames = takeoff frame − landing frame + 1), so the takeoff frame counts in both. seconds = media time; realSeconds = seconds × timeScale.
fields.sessions[].derived.intervals[].heightCm: Jump height from flight time, h = g·t²/8 with g = 9.81 m/s² and t = realSeconds. Assumes takeoff and landing at the same height.
fields.sessions[].derived.precisionMs: Real-time duration of one frame; each mark is accurate to about ±1 frame.
fields.sessions[].derived.jumps[]: One per takeoff: the flight after it and the contact before it, when there is one. incomplete = no landing marked after the takeoff yet. rsi = heightCm / 100 / contact realSeconds.
fields.sessions[].derived.unpairedMarks[]: Marks that are part of no flight or contact. reason: "out-of-sequence" = next to a mark of the same type, such as two takeoffs in a row; "alone" = no mark next to it to pair with.
fields.tables.intervals[]: One row per flight or contact interval across every session, with session context repeated on each row. index = 1-based position among intervals of the same kind within its session.
fields.tables.jumps[]: One row per jump across every session, with session context repeated on each row. index = 1-based position of the jump within its session.
fields.tables.sessions[]: One row per session with its summary statistics.
fields.tables.*[].jumpType: The owning session's jumpType, repeated on every row.
fields.recordedAt: When the video was recorded. Starts as the video file's last-modified time and may have been corrected by hand.
fields.overview: Totals and extremes across all exported sessions.
